title: 2003 AMC 10B Problem 24
statement: The first four terms in an arithmetic sequence are \(x+y,\) \(x-y,\) \(xy,\) and \(\frac{x}{y},\) in that order. What is the fifth term?

solutions.text:
The common difference is \(-2y,\) so the third and fourth terms must be \(x-3y\) and \(x-5y.\) Thus \(xy=x-3y\) and \(\dfrac{x}{y}=x-5y.\)

From \(\dfrac{x}{y}=x-5y\) we get \(x=xy-5y^2,\) and substituting \(xy=x-3y\) gives \(-3y-5y^2=0.\) Since \(y\ne 0,\) \(y=-\dfrac35\) and then \(x=-\dfrac98.\)

The fifth term is \(x-7y=-\dfrac98 + \dfrac{21}{5}=\dfrac{123}{40}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: So the third and fourth terms are \(x-3y\) and \(x-5y;\) set these equal to \(xy\) and \(\frac{x}{y}\)
